NO. 027 · Songbirds & City Birds / Dicruridae · Drongos

Black Drongo

黑卷尾 · hēi juǎn wěi Dicrurus macrocercus
Summer visitor Common 26–30 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The black bird on the wire that fights in mid-air

Black with a blue sheen, the tail ending in open scissors with the outer feathers curled up. It sits on wires and launches at anything that flies past — including raptors, which it will chase off.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • ColourAll black with blue-green metallic gloss in sunlight; bill and legs black.
  • TailLong and deeply forked, with the outermost feathers curled up at the tips — the source of the name.
  • EyeIris dark brown to dark red, hard to see in the black head.
  • ShapeSlender and upright, typically watching from a high wire or dead branch.

Behaviour

A classic sit-and-wait aerial hunter: perches high, launches fast at passing insects and returns to the same perch. Extremely aggressive, attacking raptors, crows and even people that come into its territory. A summer visitor here from April to September in farmland, villages and open woodland. The nest is a shallow cup in a fork.

Voice

Field recording

Recording Sudipto Roy · Licence CC BY-SA 3.0 · Original file

Varied, including mimicry of other birds and mechanical sounds; the usual calls are a rough 'cheer-cheer' and metallic whistles, with a loud 'kli-kli-kli' alarm.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen farmland power lines
  • Jinwan open ground
  • Tangjiawan village lanes
  • Hengqin grassland margins
Field note
A black bird that launches from a wire into mid-air, intercepts, and returns to the same wire is a drongo. Check whether the tail is forked with upturned tips.
